finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF on POST /profile/avatar: the attacker-supplied avatarUrl is fetched server-side by axios. The only check is that the string starts with 'https://', which constrains the scheme, not the destination. There is no host allowlist and no block on private, loopback, or link-local addresses. Axios follows redirects by default, so an https URL can redirect the server to plain-http internal endpoints. The response body is not returned (blind SSRF); the caller gets only the byte length.
finding.source: server.js:10 req.body.avatarUrl (route at server.js:9, no auth)

trace.note: app.post('/profile/avatar') is registered with no authentication middleware
url = req.body.avatarUrl, taken directly from the request body
validation: typeof url === 'string' and url.startsWith('https://'); scheme only, no host or IP check
await axios.get(url, ...) fetches the attacker-chosen URL; redirects are followed by default (follow-redirects, maxRedirects 5), which permits https-to-http redirects
res.json({ bytes: img.data.length }) returns only the response size (blind SSRF oracle)

finding.guards_checked: Type check (server.js:11): enforced. startsWith('https://') (server.js:11): enforced but scheme-only. Not present anywhere: host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP block, redirect restriction (maxRedirects 0 or per-hop validation), DNS-rebinding protection, auth on the route. No package.json, so the axios version and redirect default are inferred, not pinned.

verdict.guard_found: Only a scheme-only check at server.js:11 (typeof string and url.startsWith("https://")), which does not close the finding. No host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP block, redirect restriction, or auth on the route anywhere in server.js.
verdict.reason: The route at server.js:9 has no auth, the URL comes from req.body.avatarUrl at server.js:10, the only check at server.js:11 constrains scheme but not destination, and server.js:14 fetches it with axios.get while server.js:15 returns the response byte length. The redirect-to-http and axios version details are inferred since there is no package.json, but the core SSRF does not depend on them.

finding.claim: UNCERTAIN, low severity: on GET /users/:id, encodeURIComponent does not encode '.', so id='..' produces the path /v1/users/.., which normalizes to /v1/ on the fixed users.internal:8080 host. This reaches a different endpoint on the same internal service only; the host cannot be changed. Whether axios normalizes dot segments depends on the Node/axios version and is not verified.

trace.note: app.get('/users/:id') is registered with no authentication middleware
id = encodeURIComponent(req.params.id); dots are not encoded, so '..' passes through
URL built from the constant USER_SVC (server.js:7) plus the id; host is fixed, path can traverse to /v1/ if dot segments are normalized

finding.guards_checked: USER_SVC is a constant host (server.js:7): enforced. encodeURIComponent (server.js:19): enforced for '/', '?', '#'; does not handle '.' dot segments. No auth on route. Host and scheme cannot be attacker-controlled.

verdict.guard_found: server.js:7 fixes the host and scheme to http://users.internal:8080, so the attacker cannot choose the host. server.js:19 encodeURIComponent encodes '/', so the attacker cannot add path segments. Only a whole-segment '..' or '.' survives, which reaches /v1/ or /v1/users/ on the same fixed host.
verdict.reason: The trace at server.js:18-20 is accurate and req.params.id is attacker-controlled, but the host and scheme are constant (server.js:7, 20) and encodeURIComponent (server.js:19) blocks '/' so the only traversal left is to /v1/ or /v1/users/ on the same internal service, which is not an SSRF to a new target; the candidate itself rates it low and leaves axios normalization unverified.
